# Port of lib/pubid/ieee/parser.rb — the largest flavor: P-prefixed
# drafts (draft status/version/date families, =D ISO stages, /FDIS
# family), approved drafts, ANSI P forms, historical S-designations,
# corrigendum/interpretation/conformance-lead forms, multi-numbered and
# CSA dual-published identifiers, IEEE/ASTM SI/PSI, no-prefix forms,
# joint ISO/IEC/IEEE development formats, IEC/IEEE copublished labels,
# the relationship/parenthetical machinery, book nicknames, redlines,
# and title portions. The Aiee/Ire/Nesc sub-parsers are `use`d. The
# huge parse() normalization pipeline (rev/relaton/joint-stage
# spellings, entity decoding, paren balancing) is Tier-3 preprocessing
# outside the grammar. Source deviations: the duplicated
# combined_aiee_identifier branch is emitted once; "Sept"/"Sep"
# (and dotted-month) orders are lint-forced longest-first.
#
# Edition-2 conversion. The builder reads flat scalars with
# extract_value and dispatches on wrapper hashes, so leaf captures bind
# (string) and branch/wrapper captures bind (raw):
# - the zero-width markers are re-spelled as real-token captures (the
#   cie separator precedent): printed_dash_year / printed_month_year
#   capture their branch's leading separator (presence is what every
#   builder read checks), iec_label_dash captures the dash it marked,
#   the dead stage_embedded marker is dropped (nothing read it), and
#   iso_published captures the joint head choice (raw) — every read of
#   it sits behind a nil-iso_stage gate or the iso_stage elsif, so the
#   wider presence set is inert exactly where v1's was narrow.
# - the ([dash]) as draft_dash / ([rev_sep] as rev_sep) /
#   ([...] as suffix) capture-over-OPTIONAL landmines are re-spelled
#   [ (x) as y ] (parsanol-ruby#394: when the optional does not
#   participate, ruby/native omit the key but wasm emits "").
# - year_digits / digits / yearish / type_word bodies inline at every
#   capture site (a capture over a sequence/repetition rule ref expands
#   to node lists); pure literal/class alternation refs (month_name,
#   publisher, organization, dash, rev_sep...) stay refs and bind as
#   spans.
# - nested-only captures that collide with a top-level name rename with
#   the builder (a bound leak would surface the nested value where v1
#   kept the key absent): draft_date's month/year/day/dash_* ->
#   draft_date_*, the draft_version rule's dash_* -> draft_version_*,
#   fdraft's month/year -> fdraft_*, reaffirmed's year ->
#   reaffirmed_year. The builder reads the renamed keys at their nested
#   sites only.
# - the subpart run ("7.4-3-2") does NOT bind top-level: the
#   subparts[] array harvest emits empty hashes for non-firing rep
#   iterations on wasm (parsanol-ruby#399). Every subpart site — the
#   part_subpart_year alternation and the four joint/iso-draft
#   [ ((part [1*subpart])) as part_subpart_year ] slots (the canonical
#   [ (x) as y ] spelling; the glued [((x) as y)] breaks the VM parse
#   when the optional declines) — is wrapped in a part_subpart_year
#   capture bound (raw). The builder deep-collects the :subpart nodes
#   under the wrapper; raw interiors keep every capture node on both
#   engines.

use aiee
use ire
use nesc

grammar PubidIeee version "0.1.0" edition 2 {
  digit = %x30-39
  upper = %x41-5A
  lower = %x61-7A
  letter = %x41-5A / %x61-7A
  digits = 1*%x30-39
  space = " "
  dash = "-" / "–" / "–"
  dot = "."
  slash = "/"
  stage_sep = slash / "_"
  comma = ", "
  non_nl = %x01-09 / %x0B-10FFFF
  non_rparen = %x01-27 / %x2A-10FFFF
  non_rbracket = %x01-5C / %x5E-10FFFF
  non_comma_rparen = %x01-28 / %x2A-2B / %x2D-10FFFF
  non_digit_nl = %x01-09 / %x0B-2F / %x3A-10FFFF
  alnum_char = %x30-39 / %x41-5A / %x61-7A

  year_digits = (("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39))
  month_numeric = (("0" %x31-39)) / (("1" %x30-32))
  month_name = {
    "Sept." / "Oct." / "Nov." / "Dec." / "Jan." / "Feb." / "Mar." / "Apr." / "Jun." / "Jul." / "Aug." / "September" / "November" / "December" / "February" / "August" / "June" / "January" / "March" / "April" / "October" / "July" / "May" / "Sept" / "Jan" / "Feb" / "Mar" / "Apr" / "Jun" / "Jul" / "Aug" / "Sep" / "Oct" / "Nov" / "Dec"
  }

  date_with_month_text = ((month_name) as month [space] (((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)))) as year)
  date_with_month_numeric = ((((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)))) as year dash (month_numeric) as month)
  date_year_only = ((((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)))) as year)
  date_standalone = (date_with_month_text / date_with_month_numeric / date_year_only)
  organization = {
    "IEEE" / "AIEE" / "ANSI" / "ASA" / "ANS" / "IEC" / "ISO" / "ASTM" / "CSA" / "ASME" / "NACE" / "NSF" / "ASHRAE" / "NCTA" / "AESC" / "EIA" / "USEMCSC" / "AMPP" / "USAS" / "EAB" / "MPAI"
  }
  complex_org_prefix = "ANSI/IEEE-ANS" / "ANSI/IEEE" / "ANSI"
  characteristic_ieee_number = (("C" 2%x30-39 dot 1*%x30-39 *%x61-7A)) / (("802" dot 1*%x30-39 *%x61-7A)) / (("P" 1*%x30-39))
  publisher = ((complex_org_prefix)) as publisher / ((organization)) as publisher
  copublisher = {
    (("/ISO/IEC")) as copublisher / (("/IEC/ISO")) as copublisher / ((slash [space] ((organization)) as copublisher))
  }
  conformance = {
    (((([space] slash "Conformance" ((1*%x30-39)) as conf_number ([space] dash [space]) (((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)))) as conf_year)))) as conformance
  }
  ashrae_copub = {
    ((((slash "ASHRAE" space [("Guideline" space)] ((1*%x30-39)) as ashrae_number [(([space] dash [space]) (((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)))) as ashrae_year)]))) as ashrae_copub)
  }
  ieee_crossref = {
    ((((slash "C" 1*%x30-39 dot 1*%x30-39 dot 1*%x30-39 ([space] dash [space]) (((("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39))))))) as ieee_crossref)
  }
  ipcea_copub = ((((slash "IPCEA" space (1*(%x41-5A / %x61-7A / %x30-39 / "." / dash))))) as ipcea_copub)
  s_designation = {
    ([(publisher space)] [((("Draft Std" / "STD" / "Standard" / "Std No." / "Std" / "PTC" / (("N" / "n") "o.") / (("N" / "n") "o") / "No")) as type [space])] (("S" dash 1*%x30-39)) as s_number [ipcea_copub] [parenthetical])
  }
  # A dash group after the number is a PART, not more number (C1: the
  # part binds before the draft status and the year - the dash-continuation
  # swallowed "61850-9-3" whole, and the builder-side Code split came too
  # late for the separator and the P prefix).
  number = ((([("P")] *%x41-5A 1*%x30-39 *((1*%x30-39 / %x41-5A)) [%x61-7A])) as number)
  type_word = {
    "Draft Std" / "STD" / "Standard" / "Std No." / "Std" / "PTC" / (("N" / "n") "o.") / (("N" / "n") "o") / "No"
  }
  part = {
    ((dot / dash) !(("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)) (1*(!(("REV" / "Rev" / "rev")) (%x30-39 / %x41-5A / %x61-7A)))) as part
  }
  subpart = {
    ((dot / dash / "_") !(("19" / "20") 2%x30-39 0*2%x61-7A !(1*%x30-39)) (1*(!(("REV" / "Rev" / "rev")) (%x30-39 / %x61-7A)) [(dot 1*%x30-39)])) as subpart
  }
  year = (((([space] (dot / dash) [space])) date_standalone ["(E)"]))
  draft_status = ((("Active Unapproved" / "Active Approved" / "Unapproved" / "Approved" / "Active") space))
  draft_prefix = (([space] ("/" / "_" / dash / space)))
  rev_word = ("REV" / "Rev" / "rev")
  rev_sep = (dash / "_" / dot / space / slash)
  # The lettered revision id ("REVi", "REVmc") is identity - the IEEE 802
  # series letter suffix - and its separator is preserved as printed
  # ("P802.11-REVmc" renders "P802.11-Revmc"; a glued "REVi" stays glued).
  # A draft-D token after the word is the DRAFT (the "REVD2.2" family), so
  # the lettered capture declines it. The word with no id is kept as the
  # rev_bare marker ("802.1AR-Rev/D2.2").
  rev_numbered = ([rev_sep] (rev_word) [space] (1*%x30-39) as revision)
  rev_lettered = {
